**Finding submitted: IP — missing (fallback cure proposed).**

- **Investigation:** The MSA has no ownership/IP section at all. The only IP-adjacent provisions are Kubient's licence to AP of the Auction Platform (p0002 — limited, non-transferable, non-sublicensable, expressly *revocable*, and revoked on termination per p0021), Kubient's warranty that it owns the Service, Auction Platform and "products delivered hereunder" (p0040), AP's warranty of ownership of its Content and Properties (p0043) and liability for them (p0025), and the mutual trademark clause (p0065). No defined "Deliverables" or "Customer Data"; AP data flows to Kubient as "Requests" (p0011) and visitor data stored by Kubient (p0035) with no use limitation.
- **Target chosen:** fallback. Preferred-level assignment of deliverables would contradict the retained p0040 warranty that Kubient owns products delivered, requiring collateral rewrites; the fallback (Vendor keeps tools/know-how, AP gets a broad deliverables licence) is consistent with the retained bargain.
- **Cure:** one inserted paragraph 6(b) carrying exactly the eight fallback elements — Kubient retains its generic tools and know-how; AP receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business; any Kubient licence in Content, Requests or other data belonging to, supplied by or processed for AP is limited to processing solely to provide the Services. No survival, expense or procedural tails added; the new licence is not the "section 3" licence revoked under 4(c)(ii), so no dangling conflict.
